mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,300-£2,800 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. EP6DT 150hp units start around £1,300, EP6CDT 156hp units from £1,400, and 5FY 175hp units range £1,600-£2,800. Used engines start from £650. Supply & fit adds £400-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £4,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 308 1.6 THP (Prince engine) problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle (reported as early as 27,500 miles), high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure causing hard starting and misfires, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, and turbocharger oil feed line leaks. Excessive oil consumption - over 1 litre per 1,000 miles - is a common symptom of timing chain wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 308 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 308 1.6 THP values typically £2,000-£6,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,300-£2,800 represents a significant investment but often makes sense for well-maintained GT and Feline examples. For sub-£2,500 examples, a used engine from £650 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 308 1.6 THP (EP6DT/5FY) engine can reach 100,000-130,000 miles. However, HPFP failure can appear as early as 50,000 miles, and timing chain issues from 27,500-80,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct 0W-30 fully synthetic oil, timely timing chain replacement and HPFP monitoring are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 308 1.6 THP 150 and 175 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP 150 (EP6DT, 5FX) produces 150hp and was fitted to GT and Sport trims. The 1.6 THP 175 (5FY, EP6DTS) produces 175hp and was fitted to Feline and high-spec trims. Both use the same 1.6L Prince architecture, but the 5FY has a higher-output calibration and more aggressive engine mapping. The 5FY is also more susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear due to higher cylinder pressures.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine code is EP6DT (5FX) for 150hp models, EP6CDT (5FV) for 156hp models, or 5FY (EP6DTS) for 175hp models. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. The engine ECU is Bosch MED17.4. historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 308 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 308 1.6 THP (Turbo High Pressure) was the performance petrol engine for the first-generation (Phase 1, 2007-2013) 308, delivering turbocharged power to the compact family hatchback. Powered by the Prince engine family - jointly developed by PSA and BMW - the 1.6 THP featured twin-scroll turbocharging, direct injection and advanced engine management, making it one of the most exciting petrol options in the 308 range. Available in 150hp, 156hp and 175hp outputs, the 1.6 THP was fitted to Sport, GT and Feline trims. However, its complexity and well-documented reliability issues - particularly timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure and carbon buildup - have made it a significant source of replacement enquiries for owners of the 308 GT and Feline.

milestones.description: **2007** - First-generation 308 launched with 1.6 THP 150hp (EP6DT, 5FX) for GT and Sport trims
**2008** - 1.6 THP 150hp carries over with minor ECU refinements
**2009** - 1.6 THP 175hp (5FY, EP6DTS) introduced for Feline and high-spec trims
**2010** - Revised timing chain tensioner components introduced to address early failures
**2011** - HPFP and turbo oil feed line updates for improved reliability
**2012** - Final Phase 1 production; 1.6 THP continues through to 2013
**2013** - Phase 2 (EMP2 platform) launched; 1.6 THP replaced by 1.6 PureTech (EP6FDT) and 1.2 PureTech units

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EP6DT, 5FY and EP6CDT engine fitted to the Peugeot 308 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 308 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 308 1.6 THP (EP6DT/5FY) is a thrilling engine when running well, but its Prince architecture - shared with BMW and Mini - has well-documented weaknesses. Timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure, carbon buildup and turbocharger issues are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The 175hp 5FY variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear. Owners report oil consumption of over 1 litre per 1,000 miles on some 1.6 THP engines, which is often a symptom of timing chain wear. Every rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 THP Engines Rattle and Fail
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. The 1.6 THP is also known for excessive oil consumption, which is often a symptom of timing chain wear. Peugeot released a TSB with revised tensioner and guide parts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure; many owners report needing replacement twice

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage; replacement costs can reach £2,500-£3,500 when major internal damage occurs

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 308 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle, address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 km) with fully synthetic 0W-30 oil are critical to preventing timing chain guide wear.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6DT/5FY Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 THP Engines Fail to Start and Run Roughly
problems.rootCause: The Bosch HPFP's internal cam follower wears prematurely, causing metal contamination to circulate through the high-pressure fuel rail and injectors. Symptoms include hard starting, rough idle, misfires and, in severe cases, complete non-start. Fault codes P0087 and P1336-P1340 are common indicators. The 5FY 175hp variant is particularly susceptible due to higher fuel pressures. Early-series engines (before 2011) are most affected.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, flush fuel lines, replace inline filter
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before metal debris reaches injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full rebuild with upgraded HPFP and cleaned rail, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Essential when metallic particles have contaminated the combustion chambers

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 308 1.6 THP is catastrophic if delayed. If diagnostic codes show fuel rail pressure deviation alongside metallic fuel, budget for a full engine replacement immediately - repairing injectors alone will not prevent repeat failure. The 5FY 175hp variant is especially susceptible; HPFP failure is one of the most common reasons for 308 1.6 THP engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Find specialist Peugeot 308 1.6 THP rebuilt engines with upgraded HPFP

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption. Owners report misfire codes (P1336, P1337, P1339, P1340) on cold start, with the engine struggling and then dying.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Oil Feed Issues - Additional Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger's oil feed line can leak or become restricted, starving the turbo of lubrication and leading to bearing failure. Carbon deposits in the turbo can also cause wastegate sticking. Fault codes P0033 (turbocharger bypass solenoid circuit) and P107A (wastegate) are common indicators. The 5FY 175hp variant places additional stress on the turbo system. Loss of power and black smoke are typical symptoms.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of turbocharger and oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new turbo and oil feed system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 308 1.6 THP has turbo lag or blue smoke, have the oil feed lines inspected immediately. Replacing these components early can prevent catastrophic turbo failure. Once turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, a full rebuilt engine is the safest option. Turbocharger failures have been reported on the 1.6 THP due to poor bearing lubrication.
